title: WALL-SS: Scaling Long-horizon World Models via Next-Scale Autoregression
paper_type_rationale: World model with a new autoregressive paradigm (next-scale AR) plus three contributions: action-conditioned next-scale prediction, scale-compressed long-horizon memory, on-policy alignment. New state-of-the-art on quantitative metrics + real robot.

central_claims.claim: Next-scale autoregression (coarse→fine × time) extends next-token AR to support long-horizon visual generation with bounded memory.
supporting_evidence: Table 1 整体 13 项指标中 11 项最高
Figure 14 平均 Task Progress 69.1 vs 最强基线 49.6
Figure 1 中心 'Coarse → Mid → Fine' 尺度金字塔 + Bounded Time-scale Memory 4 桶
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Wall-SS 的 next-scale AR 范式在长视频生成 + 闭环控制上同时优于扩散与 next-token AR。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 该范式在 Motion Smoothness(-9.8%)与跨 embodiment 迁移上的表现未知。

central_claims.claim: Action-conditioned next-scale prediction 在每一尺度层显式注入尺度对齐动作,使 Action Following 与 Trajectory Accuracy 数量级跃升。
supporting_evidence: Table 1 Action Following 0.290 vs 0.044(基线 Cosmos3-Nano)+559%
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: 动作信号需要被显式注入到每个尺度层级,而不是作为全局条件均匀稀释。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: Action Following 0.290 仍远低于 1.0,完全动作跟随仍未解决。

central_claims.claim: Scale-compressed memory (4 桶:Anchor/Distant/Mid/Recent) 让有界显存支持分钟级流式展开。
supporting_evidence: Figure 1 中央 'Bounded Time-scale Memory' 模块
Figure 3 主干中 Time-Scale KV Memory 4 桶结构
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: 时间尺度压缩记忆可作为长视频世界模型的可行 KV 缓存方案。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 在显存严格受限(单卡 <40GB)场景的可行性未验证;跨小时级生成的可行性未验证。

central_claims.claim: On-policy alignment 用 PPO/GRPO + Reference KL + AR Replay 改善动作漂移与长时程不一致,且保留视觉分布。
supporting_evidence: Figure 6 定性:30s/60s 帧 WALL-SS 仍绿框成功,基线全红框失败
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: 同策略视觉对齐不会摧毁预训练视觉分布,且对长时程鲁棒性有显著改善。
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: 如果 evaluator 与 actor 同源(或共享 backbone),FPR 会否飙升未知;evaluator 选型的最佳实践未给出。

claim_boundaries: Action Following 0.290 absolute — still well below 1.0 (i.e., not solved, just 6.6x better than prior).
Motion Smoothness regressed (-9.8%) — coarse-to-fine may introduce mild jitter.
Closed-loop task progress avg 69.1 vs 49.6 best baseline — gap closes on simple tasks but stays on long-history ones.
On-policy alignment relies on evaluator quality — if the evaluator is optimistic (false-positive rate 0.136), optimization could promote weak checkpoints.
negative_or_limiting_results: Motion Smoothness 0.715 vs Wan2.2-14B 0.793 (-9.8%) — sole regression among 13 metrics
Conditional transition bias +0.12 on insertion tasks (contact-intensive stages)
False-positive rate 0.136 — generated rollouts over-predict success when real failed

mechanism_result_map.result: reduces action drift + long-horizon inconsistency (qualitative Fig 6)

comparative_positioning: Among world-model + VLA baselines: out-performs DreamZero (44.1), pi0.5 (49.6), LingBot-VA (34.0) on task progress. Among video generation baselines: 12/13 metrics best, only Motion Smoothness lost. Implies WALL-SS sits at the intersection of 'large video model' and 'action-relevant world model', unlike pure video models that fail on action following.
reuse_takeaways: Scale-wise autoregression + bounded time-scale memory is a credible alternative to next-token video diffusion for long-horizon generation.
Action following is the dimension where world models most need to beat diffusion — quantitative gap here is the most decisive test.
On-policy alignment requires careful evaluator design — false-positive rate is a leading indicator of self-bias.
followup_questions: Can the next-scale AR paradigm be combined with a large VLA head for closed-loop deployment without retraining?
What is the scaling law across scales (not tokens) — how does performance grow with #scales vs #params?
How transferable is the pre-trained WALL-SS backbone to non-X2 robot embodiments?
